strategic implementation, and stockpile of medical countermeasures (MCMs) (e.g., vaccines and adjuvants) for pandemic preparedness and response. The Pandemic Vaccines and Adjuvants Program works to accelerate pandemic response timelines by managing the U.S. National Pre-Pandemic Influenza Vaccine Stockpile (NPIVS) and implementing its strategic use in the event of a public health emergency. The NPIVS maintains a robust library of influenza virus vaccine seeds and ensures sufficient pre-pandemic antigens and adjuvants to rapidly formulate enough vaccine doses to immunize critical care workers and at-risk populations early during a response. Our team strives to ensure vaccine implementation strategies are nimble and robust datasets are available to demonstrate vaccines are safe and immunogenic to inform pandemic preparedness strategy and policy decisions. Christine Oshansky, Ph.D. IEID Pandemic Vaccines and Adjuvants Program Director Christine Oshansky, Ph.D. IEID Pandemic Vaccines and Adjuvants Program Director Pandemic Vaccines And Adjuvants INVESTMENT AREAS Select Investment Area to Learn More Pandemic Preparedness and Response Pandemic Influenza Vaccine Manufacturing Readiness Inventory of Pre-pandemic Vaccines and Adjuvants Vaccine Implementation Strategies Pandemic Preparedness and Response The U.S. National Pre-Pandemic Influenza Vaccine Stockpile (NPIVS) Program, established in 2005 and overseen by BARDA: Manages production and evaluates vaccine implementation of stored MCMs for pandemic preparedness and response or as required in response to a U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)-designated Public Health Emergency. Procures vaccines against influenza viruses and strains with pandemic potential. Supports U.S. government efforts to modernize influenza virus vaccines. The goal of the NPIVS focuses on achieving faster and better production of pandemic influenza vaccines. Faster: Reduce time from sequence identification of any influenza virus strain of interest to availability of first vaccine doses Reduce time to produce and deliver more vaccine doses Better: Expand vaccine delivery options Decrease required vaccine antigen and adjuvant dose (e.g., dose sparing), thereby increasing pandemic vaccine availability Define national vaccination implementation strategies (e.g., mix-and-match antigen and adjuvants) The NPIVS utilizes the HHS Influenza Risk Assessment Tool (IRAT), run by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to identify and evaluate potential pandemic influenza virus threats. IRAT results aid BARDA/NPIVS to implement measured responses from candidate virus vaccines, virus vaccine seeds, clinical investigational lots, the commercial scaling of vaccine manufacturing for stockpiling or response, and the support of clinical safety and immunogenicity trials. The quality of stockpiled vaccines is routinely evaluated through vaccine potency assays as part of master stability programs, which allows readiness to fill/finish pandemic vaccines in case of need. BARDA establishes industry and interagency partnerships to strengthen preparedness and rapid response capabilities for influenza pandemics. Pandemic Influenza Vaccine Manufacturing Readiness A strong domestic vaccine manufacturing capability is critical for bolstering national security and responding to seasonal and pandemic influenza. BARDA supports the establishment and expansion of domestic manufacturing facilities, which are vital to an effective and rapid pandemic response. The Pandemic Vaccines and Adjuvants Program and Division of Pharmaceutical Countermeasures and Infrastructure (PCI) work in partnership with influenza vaccine manufacturing facilities to support pandemic readiness in order to deliver enough doses to vaccinate the U.S. population during an emergency. Partnership efforts aim to increase domestic manufacturing capacity through the following: Warm-basing domestic manufacturing facilities (e.g., enabling the ability to provide at least 150 million doses of cell-based pandemic influenza vaccine within six months of an influenza pandemic declaration; to increase adjuvant manufacturing). Supplying eggs and other essential vaccine components/supplies year-round. Retrofitting influenza vaccine manufacturing facilities for adjuvant production (see Influenza and EID Vaccine Development Program page for more details). Increasing overall adjuvant manufacturing production. Together, these approaches help to ensure the nation is prepared to mount an effective and swift response to a potential pandemic influenza threat. Inventory of Pre-pandemic Vaccines and Adjuvants To effectively prepare and respond to future influenza pandemic threats, BARDA has established and maintains the NPIVS, which is composed of adjuvants and pre-pandemic H2Nx, H5Nx, H7Nx, H9Nx, H1N1v, and H3N2v vaccine virus seeds and/or bulk antigens. As part of HHS influenza pandemic preparedness and response activities, BARDA acquires pandemic vaccine candidates and conducts clinical studies to collect data to support an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) or a license application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). To shorten timelines for making vaccines available to immunize the U.S. population, HHS has supported the expansion of domestic vaccine manufacturing capacity, including the use of adjuvanted vaccines and the licensure of seasonal cell-based and recombinant influenza vaccines. Vaccine Implementation Strategies Since the inception of the NPIVS, clinical studies have been conducted by BARDA, and in partnership with NIAID-NIH, to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of stockpiled vaccines. Of note, the “mix and match studies,” which began in 2009, clinically evaluates combinations of antigens and adjuvants manufactured by different companies and includes heterologous antigen prime and boost vaccination strategies. In addition, cross-reactivity studies of sera from people immunized with the stockpiled antigens are measured against previous and circulating influenza viruses with pandemic potential. Results from these studies are used to continuously shape the composition of the NPIVS by adding antigens against new emerging strains and subtypes and support pre-EUA and EUA regulatory submissions, thereby enabling the NPIVS to continue supporting the speed and efficiency of a response against a potential pandemic threat. Studies include clinical evaluation of the safety and immunogenicity of NPIVS candidate vaccines and adjuvant systems to support antigen and adjuvant sparing as well as dose sparing, which are crucial for mass vaccination during a pandemic event.
